old: From US-2 at Coles Corner take SR-207 north, then Chiwawa River Road (FR-62) about 22 miles and Phelps Creek Road (FR-6211) about 2.3 miles to the Phelps Creek Trailhead. Chiwawa River Road and Phelps Creek Road have been closed since August 2026 for the Little Giant Fire; check the road status before you go.
text: From US-2 at Coles Corner take SR-207 north, then Chiwawa River Road (FR-62) about 22 miles and Phelps Creek Road (FR-6211) about 2.3 miles to the Phelps Creek Trailhead. Chiwawa River Road is closed to vehicles north of the Atkinson Flats Campground junction by a storm-damage order from May 20, 2026 through December 31, 2027, unless lifted sooner, so the trailhead cannot be reached by car; check the road status before you go.
why: Forest Service storm-damaged roads order (start May 20 2026, end Dec 31 2027, updated Jul 27 2026) closes FSR 6200 from Atkinson Flats north toward Trinity and lists Phelps Creek Trailhead as affected; the Little Giant Fire order (reduced Oct 14) runs only through Oct 31 2026. Checked twice (researcher + my fetch).

old: From Glacier, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (Forest Road 39), turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (Forest Road 37) and follow it 12.7 miles to the trailhead at the end of the road. Deadhorse Road is closed to vehicles at mile 3.1 by flood damage, a closure still in effect in June 2026; check the road status before you go.
text: From Glacier, drive Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542) east about 1 mile past the Glacier Public Service Center to Glacier Creek Road (Forest Road 39), turn right, then take an immediate left onto Deadhorse Road (Forest Road 37) and follow it 12.7 miles to the trailhead at the end of the road. Since June 2026 Deadhorse Road has been closed at its start until further notice while flood damage is repaired; check the road status before you go.
why: Forest Service alert (start/updated Jun 1 2026): FSR 37 closed at mile 0.03 until further notice for flood-damage repair. No page supports 'mile 3.1'.

old: From the Mountain Loop Highway near milepost 7, turn onto Tupso Pass Road (Forest Road 41). The road is washed out about 4.8 miles in and closed to vehicles beyond, so the trailhead at its end is reached only on foot or by bike.
text: From the Mountain Loop Highway near milepost 7, turn onto Tupso Pass Road (Forest Road 41). The road is washed out about 4.8 miles in and closed to vehicles beyond, so the trailhead at its end is reached only on foot or by bike. From September 29 through December 31, 2026 the road is also closed to all traffic from the Forest Road 4110 junction for timber operations.
why: Forest Service order (Sep 29-Dec 31 2026, updated Oct 1 2026): FSR 41 closed from the FSR 4110 intersection for timber operations, Three Fingers Lookout and Trail 641 affected. WTA confirms the 4.8-mile washout and the closure at FR 4110.

old: From US-2 at Skykomish, turn north onto Beckler River Road (FR-65) and drive about 12.5 miles to Jack Pass, take the second left and go 2.3 miles to FR-63, then turn right and go 4.2 miles to the large parking area at the North Fork Skykomish trailhead. Beckler River Road has been reported closed to vehicles by flood damage since December 2025.
text: From US-2 at Skykomish, turn north onto Beckler River Road (FR-65) and drive about 12.5 miles to Jack Pass, take the second left and go 2.3 miles to FR-63, then turn right and go 4.2 miles to the large parking area at the North Fork Skykomish trailhead. Since the December 2025 floods Beckler River Road has been closed beyond Jack Pass and the North Fork Skykomish bridge on FR-63 is out, so the trailhead cannot be reached by car right now.
why: Forest Service Skykomish road damage alert (Jun 30 2026): FR 65 graded to MP 12.3 at Jack Pass, closed after; FR 63 undrivable from the 65 side (North Fork Skykomish bridge out). Snohomish County: Index-Galena closed MP 10-14 since Dec 2025.

old: Drive US-2 to Skykomish, then north on Beckler River Road (FR-65) for about 15 miles; turn left (west) onto FR-63 and follow it about 4.6 miles to where it crosses the North Fork Skykomish River again; park at the unmarked pullout on the rise just past the bridge, about a mile east of Galena. Beckler River Road has been reported closed to vehicles by flood damage since December 2025.
text: Drive US-2 to Skykomish, then north on Beckler River Road (FR-65) for about 15 miles; turn left (west) onto FR-63 and follow it about 4.6 miles to where it crosses the North Fork Skykomish River again; park at the unmarked pullout on the rise just past the bridge, about a mile east of Galena. why: Same Forest Service alert as above.

old: From the end of FS spur NF-6514-410 off Beckler River Road (FR-65). Beckler River Road has been reported closed to vehicles by flood damage since December 2025.
text: From the end of FS spur NF-6514-410 off Beckler River Road (FR-65). Since the December 2025 floods Eagle Creek Road (FR-6514) has been gated at its start, with a blown-out culvert beyond, so the spur cannot be reached by car right now.
why: Forest Service Skykomish alert (Jun 30 2026): FSR 6514 Eagle Creek Road gate closed at MP 0, blown culvert MP 1.6. FR 65 itself is open to MP 12.3.

old: Via Beckler River Road (FR-65) into the FR-6510/6514/6517 spur network to road's end ~0.5 mile east of the summit. Beckler River Road has been reported closed to vehicles by flood damage since December 2025.
text: Via Beckler River Road (FR-65) into the FR-6510/6514/6517 spur network to road's end ~0.5 mile east of the summit. Since the December 2025 floods Eagle Creek Road (FR-6514) has been gated at its start and FR-6510 at milepost 1, so the road end cannot be reached by car right now.
why: Forest Service Skykomish alert (Jun 30 2026): FSR 6510 closed at gate MP 1.0 (culvert out MP 1.2, bridge out MP 2); FSR 6514 gate closed MP 0.

old: From Seattle take Interstate 90 east over the Columbia River past Vantage to exit 143, turn left onto Silica Road, pass beneath the freeway, then turn left at the first chance onto Vantage Road and follow it 1.4 miles down the canyon to parking on the left. A Discover Pass is required. As of May 2026 the area was reported effectively closed because of problems with the main road in.
text: From Seattle take Interstate 90 east over the Columbia River past Vantage to exit 143, turn left onto Silica Road, pass beneath the freeway, then turn left at the first chance onto Vantage Road and follow it 1.4 miles down the canyon to parking on the left. A Discover Pass is required. Since May 2026 rockslides have closed Vantage Road, so the parking cannot be reached by car; check the road status before you go.
why: Columbia Basin Herald May 16 2026: Vantage Road SW closed west of Silica Road by rockslides until further notice (Grant County Sheriff); WTA Frenchman Coulee alert 7.21.26: road to the trailhead closed by rockfall.

old: The Elbow Lake trailhead is about 11 miles up Forest Road 38 off Mosquito Lake Road, and the road is gated December 1 to June 15 for elk winter range. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.
text: The Elbow Lake trailhead is about 11 miles up Forest Road 38 off Mosquito Lake Road, and the road past mile 9 is closed each year from December 1 to June 15. Since July 2026 Forest Road 38 has been closed to vehicles by a washout at milepost 7.
why: No page supports the elk-winter-range reason; the seasonal 12/01-6/15 closure past mile 9 is stated by the road's own trail listing. Washout at MP 7 confirmed by the Forest Service alert (Jul 27 2026).
